last.verdict: Opendoor bought far more homes than it sold, and it now expects Q4 operating losses to widen to $70M–$85M as profit per home sold falls.

takeaways.label: Profit shrinking, losses widening
takeaways.text: Contribution margin fell to 3.3% from 5.8% last quarter, below the 4%–4.5% guide. Q4 contribution profit is guided lower again, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $70M–$85M versus $31M now.

takeaways.label: Inventory and debt ballooning
takeaways.text: Homes in inventory hit 7,596 (3,139 a year ago) after 4,865 purchases. Inventory is $2.6B, and $2.0B of home-loan debt is now due within a year.

takeaways.label: Growth missed, but guided higher
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 12% to $1.02B, short of the 20%+ target. Q4 revenue is guided up at least 40%, selling into what the company calls a difficult market.

takeaways.label: Profit goal slipping
takeaways.text: Management says it is behind its goal of positive adjusted net income by end of 2026, blaming a slower housing market. Net loss was $218M.

history.verdict: Investors sold on a weak margin outlook despite revenue and cash-burn improvement.

reasons.label: Lower margin outlook
reasons.text: Next-quarter contribution margin guided to 4%–4.5%, below this quarter's 5.8%, blamed on seasonality.

reasons.label: Sales far below last year
reasons.text: Revenue was $883M, down about 44% from a year ago, and below analyst estimates.

reasons.label: Bigger loss, mostly stock pay
reasons.text: Net loss was $162M versus $29M a year ago, driven by about $119M of stock-based pay.
